description: This is a solo team! I'm a student interested in astronomy and aerospace, and am well-versed in Python and programming.
summary: This project is Analog Atlas, a dashboard that consolidates data regarding various Earth analog sites, conditions expected for Mars and Moon habitats, and factors associated with these locations. It provides a visual understanding of analog sites and how they rank by the user's preferred factors, allowing them to see which Earth analog site would be the best choice to study further for a potential base on the Moon/Mars.
details:
My project is called Analog Atlas, a tool that can be used to map out various Earth analog sites and check whether or not their conditions are compatible with the target location for sustainable base-building on the Moon and Mars. The user can import their own data (sample data file provided in Github to download and try) or use the present data. There is a map model that shows the different Earth analogs ranked based on compatability in various factors, such as mean surface temperature, elevation, precipitation, and more. Additionally, the application includes radar charts for all the analog sites on Earth to show the relationships between the different factors being compared as well as descriptions of the strengths/weaknesses of a location. The user is also able to choose the target conditions they are planning for regarding habitation of the Moon/Mars - changing these influences the compatability ranking, and demonstrates which Earth analog site would be better suited for observation and study.

This project is intended to create a simple visual interface for researchers and scientists looking to study Earth analog sites and understand how it can resemble a Moon/Mars habitat site. During the development stages, I considered factors such as convenience for researchers working on this challenge in real-time, visual understanding, specificity, and flexibility. The app allows user freedom, meaning that the operator can choose which factors to focus on and save time in seeing which sites are most compatible for the given situation.

For this project, I primarily used Python libraries (e.g. astropy, numpy, planetary-computer, rasterio) for data input and processing, Google Fonts for stylistic text fonts used in the application, Visual Studio Code Editor, and Claude AI (for assistance with prototype and data pipeline building). I am also using Github to store all of my data and host the web application on a Pages website.
